tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Diagnose...', 'Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms and intents (job denied access, fails with X error, stalls, pipeline registers no model package, etc.), explicitly lists many trigger contexts covering both training and registry domains, and also explicitly excludes an adjacent case (evaluation jobs). It is dense but remains a tightly packed paragraph consistent with a complex, multi-faceted skill, listing triggers rather than implementation internals.
tests.evidence: "Diagnose an Amazon SageMaker training or customization job... Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity, ResourceLimitExceeded or out of memory, goes to Failed with no logs..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense with domain-specific, non-obvious procedures (SageMaker training failure buckets, Model Registry governance checks, check-id taxonomy) and does not explain general concepts the agent already knows. It is fairly long, but nearly every sentence carries skill-specific content rather than generic exposition.
tests.evidence: "The capacity-vs-quota split is opposite remediations: read both the FailureReason and the quota value"

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed check catalogs, API quirks, known causes, and collection details are all pushed into references/ files; the body only contains a compact index table and router table pointing to them, not the full detection rules/remediations/citations.
tests.evidence: "The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference; the table below is a what-it-catches index."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files (api-quirks.md, checks-sagemaker-training.md, collection-reference.md, known-causes.md, metrics-and-logs.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by explicit triggering conditions describing when to load it.
tests.evidence: "Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom (training §1–§7, Model Registry §8–§14)"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (failure classification, severity assignment, read-only guardrails) are given exact prescriptive steps, while flexible areas (how to assemble the final narrative, how to phrase remediation) are left open with rationale given.
tests.evidence: "Bucket the FailureReason into exactly one cause and cite the check... The capacity-vs-quota split is opposite remediations: read both the FailureReason and the quota value"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal choices; it directs specific APIs per symptom in the router table without alternatives framed as equal options.
tests.evidence: "DescribeTrainingJob FailureReason and SecondaryStatus" — a single designated API per symptom row, no competing alternatives listed as equals

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The review procedure teaches a generalizable classification/diagnosis approach (identify area, classify pending vs failed, bucket failure reason, confirm artifact, review governance) applicable to any training job or model package, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: "Classify before prescribing anything. Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist... Step 4: Bucket the FailureReason into exactly one cause."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an extensive 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' section listing non-obvious traps and misleading API responses, functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: "'The job is InProgress with Pending, so it is failing.' A job waiting on GPU capacity is control-plane-healthy, not Failed."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured health reports and provides dedicated templates in assets/ for both training and registry reports.
tests.evidence: "[training-job-health-report-template.md](assets/training-job-health-report-template.md) (load when a full training report is requested)"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline templates exist in the body; actual templates are stored in assets/ and referenced conditionally.
tests.evidence: No inline template blocks found in the body; templates are only linked via assets/ references

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Both asset files are referenced in the body via markdown links in the Step 7 and Appendix sections.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Asset links specify the triggering condition for loading them (when a full report of that area is requested).
tests.evidence: "(load when a full training report is requested)"

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: Asset references use relative paths rooted at assets/ without absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with Step N labels, and the detailed subsections below it use matching '### Step N —' headings that reference the same step numbers.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Identify the area..." paired with "### Step 1 — Identify the area"

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation gate ('Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output') instructing the agent to check check-id accuracy, observed vs inferred values, severity correctness, and masking before presenting findings.
tests.evidence: "A wrong or unsupported finding is worse than a slow one. Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
